item.title: Missy Elliott Tells Dancers They’re Artists As Cancer Gala Raises Over $760K
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Missy Elliott honored dancers in her Icon Award speech as the Gala of the Stars raised more than $760,000 for cancer support.
item.content:encoded:
Missy Elliott put dancers at the center of her Icon Award speech earlier this week, calling them artists rather than stage props.

The rapper accepted the honor at the October 22 Gala of the Stars at The Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills, California. The benefit raised more than $760,000 for Dancers Against Cancer, organizers said in a release.

Janet Jackson, who received the same honor in 2025, presented Missy with the award. Missy’s acceptance speech focused on the work that dancers bring to an artist’s show.

“Dancers are not just props on a stage behind artists. What y’all give is energy, emotion, expression, excitement, entertainment to an artist’s show. You bring life to an artist’s lyrics on that stage. Y’all are artists too! Because it takes incredible skill, dedication, discipline, practice and passion to do what you do,” Missy said.

Jackson’s presentation touched on that same bond between the music and the people who bring it to the stage.

“Missy Elliott helped make dancers impossible to ignore,” Jackson said. She credited Missy with elevating choreography and encouraging dancers to embrace their individuality.

At Thursday’s gala, Anthony Kanec performed a dance tribute to Missy. Maks Chmerkovskiy hosted the benefit, which also honored Toni Basil with its Lifetime Achievement Award and Vincent Paterson with its Vanguard Award.

Paula Abdul presented the Paula Abdul Legacy Award in a posthumous tribute to Chita Rivera. Hilaria Baldwin received the Philanthropist of the Year Award.

Organizers said the money raised would help dancers, choreographers, educators, and their families affected by cancer.

item.title: Kohen Wiley’s Family Pushes Back As Experts Fault Police Tactics
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kohen Wiley's family challenged the state's shooting decision as experts questioned why an officer stepped into danger.
item.content:encoded:
Kohen Wiley’s family is not ready to accept the state’s decision to clear the officer who killed their 1-year-old boy, saying the video shows police used force they didn’t need to use.

Mississippi released new video October 22, including footage from Sgt. Hunter Foster’s camera. Foster shot into a moving car during a June 14 shoplifting call at a Senatobia Walmart, killing Kohen.

At a news conference, family lawyer Ben Crump said police went too far before shots were fired. “Police never should have drawn their weapons for a misdemeanor shoplifting investigation,” he said, according to WMC.

Fellow family lawyer Van Turner said the key question was whether the car posed an imminent threat. He said officers had not taken proper care.

Six experts who reviewed video for a Mississippi Today report said an officer put himself at risk when he stepped in front of the car. That went against training that tells police to move aside.

The fight for answers began months ago. In June, community members organized a Walmart boycott and pushed for the release of video. ABC24 Memphis also covered Kohen’s mother’s response then.

But the expert review had limits. Mississippi Today and its partner, The New York Times, sought views on incomplete footage leaked before the state released it. The experts could not tell whether the car hit any officer.

“It’s just a tragedy. It could have been avoided. You don’t stand in front of the car, period. You stand off to the side,” said Chuck Wexler, who heads a group that advises police on use of force.

David Mastagni, a lawyer who defends police and also reviewed the footage, disagreed with the critics. He said replaying video does not show what an officer feels in the moment.

Foster’s lawyer, Martin Zummach, says the car put his client in danger and left him with “no choice” but to shoot, The Associated Press reported. The family is seeking a federal probe.

Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch’s office found the shooting justified on October 19 and declined to file charges.

For Kohen’s grandmother, Veronica Roberson, that finding brought no peace. “The word ‘justified’ has haunted me,” she said.

item.title: Usher Launches Paid USC Fellowships Beyond The Stage
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Usher's New Look teamed with USC Thornton for paid fellowships that put five students behind the scenes of live entertainment.
item.content:encoded:
Usher‘s nonprofit is giving five USC students a year behind the scenes of live entertainment through paid fellowships that go beyond a single internship desk.

Usher’s New Look and the USC Thornton School of Music announced their Founding Fellows program Friday, October 23. The undergraduate students will learn from people working in touring, production, venues, artist management and the business of putting on major shows.

The five students were chosen through a competitive application process. Each receives a stipend, and the program also supports travel and a final individual project.

They began their work in September with a leadership session led by New Look co-founder Shawn H. Wilson. The students then visited the “R&B Tour” at SoFi Stadium, learning alongside interns already working within the touring operation.

Rather than train for one job at one company, the fellows will follow a personal question across several parts of the industry. They will use those experiences to figure out where their own skills fit.

The fellowship builds on New Look’s work connecting young adults with jobs beyond the stage. Earlier this year, its touring internship put students to work in audio, wardrobe and multimedia during Usher and Chris Brown’s stadium run.

New Look’s 2025 Entertainment Industry Club recap offers a look at its earlier training work.

The touring internship produced concrete results. UATL reported in August that it hired six interns after two and a half months of work at 18 tour stops. Their duties included running cables, preparing stage equipment and photographing fans. One participant, Mi’Cai Haywood, was already studying at USC Thornton.

The new fellowship creates a separate route for university students while bringing them together with young professionals from Atlanta and Detroit.

The program’s next stop is a visit to Los Angeles. Organizers are developing a November trip to Detroit around the Motown Museum, Michigan Central and Detroit Spark Lab, connecting music history with present-day training and technology.

Organizers also plan a Las Vegas visit in early 2027 focused on Metallica, Live Nation and Sphere. That portion would explore the teams behind immersive live shows, from sound and images to production and venue operations.

The fellows will finish in spring 2027 with individual projects based on what they learned and how they plan to use it.

item.title: Compton Menace Generates Concern Grew Over His Health
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Compton Menace had fans concerned over his health, creating a lot of speculation.
item.content:encoded:
Compton Menace has people concerned. The West Coast rapper’s health is front and center right now.

Multiple posts circulating online suggest the rapper was involved in a motorcycle crash that left him injured. The reports show he’s loved also since there is plenty of support and concern for the artist.

C-Menace may have suffered a fractured leg or a broken one. We do not have any real medical update so there are more questions than answers.

Where did the accident happen? How serious was the crash? Was anyone else involved? And perhaps most importantly, how is Compton Menace doing? We do not know. I have heard a lot, including he’s more seriously injured so we have to wait and see.

Menace, whose real name is Michael Joseph Taylor, has been a recognizable figure in West Coast Hip-Hop for years. His association with The Game and the Black Wall Street movement helped introduce him to a broader audience and the movie Straight Outta Compton immortalized him.

Motorcycle accidents can result in serious injuries, but everything is pretty unclear. The situation remains developing, with social media currently serving as the primary source of information.

AllHipHop is following the reports and looking for additional information about Menace’s condition.

For now, lets hope Compton rapper is on the road to recovery.

The West Coast Hip-Hop community and all of us have watched Menace build his career through music, acting and industry relationships. 

We wish Compton Menace a full and speedy recovery.

item.title: Nicki Minaj Says New Answers Undercut Ex-Employee’s $3,900 Demand
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nicki Minaj challenged Brandon Garrett's $3,900 request, saying her later answers undercut his motion in their assault lawsuit.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj asked a judge to reject her ex-manager’s $3,900 sanctions request, arguing she had already supplied the answers her former employee wanted.

Garrett sued Minaj and her company, Pink Personality, in January 2025 for assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress.

His complaint claimed the rapper attacked him backstage at Detroit’s Little Caesars Arena on April 21, 2024, during her “Pink Friday 2 World Tour.”

Earlier this week, her lawyers said they answered six sets of written questions in July, met with Brandon Garrett’s attorneys in August and supplied more answers in September, MyNewsLA reported.

“(Garrett) should be barred from using the outdated motions to compel further responses after the verified further responses were served in July,” her lawyers wrote.

They argued that Garrett missed the deadline to challenge those responses. His $3,900 request sought to cover legal costs for bringing the discovery motion.

Garrett’s lawyers had complained that Minaj missed a February deadline and supplied inadequate answers in March. They wanted facts backing her denials about threats to his safety, lost wages and emotional harm.

Garrett said the dispute began after Minaj learned he had asked another employee to collect her prescriptions. Garrett said he delegated the errand because he was helping her change clothes for the show.

He alleged Minaj struck his face and wrist, knocking off his hat. Garrett said he then locked himself in a bathroom and later reported the incident to police. He sought damages to be determined at trial.

Minaj denied the claims through attorney Judd Burstein, who called the reported lawsuit “completely false and frivolous” when it emerged in January 2025.

The allegations also drew a police investigation.

FOX 2 Detroit reported on January 6, 2025, that Wayne County prosecutors declined a warrant request, saying there was insufficient evidence of a crime. They asked Detroit police to investigate further.

Judge Eric Harmon is scheduled to hear the discovery dispute on November 10 in Los Angeles Superior Court.

item.title: Burna Boy & Davido Shake Hands At Zlatan’s Bachelor Party
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Burna Boy and Davido shook hands at Zlatan Ibile's bachelor party in Lagos ahead of the rapper's October 24 wedding.
item.content:encoded:
Burna Boy and Davido shook hands at Zlatan Ibile’s bachelor party in Lagos, bringing the two Afrobeats stars together after years of public tension.

The greeting took place at a nightclub, according to Pulse Nigeria. The outlet reported that footage showed the singers shaking hands during the celebration ahead of Zlatan’s wedding to Davita Lamai.

The handshake prompted talk of a truce, but neither singer had addressed the encounter.

Zlatan has worked with both men. Davido appeared on the rapper’s “Osanle” in November 2018, a Fresh VDM production. Zlatan and Burna Boy followed with the video for “Killin Dem” in January 2019.

“Killin Dem” earned Best Collabo at the 2019 Headies and appeared on Burna Boy’s “African Giant” album. Kel P produced the track. The official video below comes from that earlier collaboration.

Burna Boy and Davido’s own relationship also stretched back well before the public disputes. Davido said the two met in 2010. He recalled spending time with Burna Boy before they were well known and said he had rooted for his success.

“Burna Boy and I are brothers,” Davido said.

@xdyaps OBO & Odogwu are besties again 🙈 #greenscreen #yapper #yapping #burnaboy #davido ♬ original sound – Yaps

Davido also denied that his song “FEM” was aimed specifically at Burna Boy. Listeners had connected the record to their dispute because it used Odogwu, a name associated with Burna Boy. He described the mention as an invitation for Burna Boy to call him and join him at a party.

That interview also showed how frustrated Davido had become with the dispute. He said he had tried to talk with Burna Boy several times and maintained that he had never tried to discredit him.

Burna Boy later said the two had settled their differences in a post.

“FYI, I have no issues with David. We good now,” he wrote. Burna Boy also called for people to show each other love as they headed into 2022.

Zlatan and Lamai’s wedding is scheduled for Saturday, October 24.

item.title: Bhad Bhabie Wants $6.9 Million For Home She Bought In Cash
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Bhad Bhabie seeks a buyer for her Boca Raton estate as her property portfolio, subscription income and latest music take focus.
item.content:encoded:
Bhad Bhabie wants $6.9 million for her Florida mansion after banking an OnlyFans fortune, but she’s asking far less than before.

The rapper listed her Boca Raton property Wednesday, according to TMZ, with seven bedrooms spread across 8,958 square feet. A pool, sauna and six-car garage sit on the gated acre, along with a guesthouse spread across two stories.

She sought $7.89 million for the estate in 2023, putting this asking price $990,000 below that earlier figure. Still, she’s seeking $800,000 above the $6.1 million she paid in 2022 before accounting for fees, upkeep and other costs.

The purchase was reportedly an all-cash deal with NFL player Jason Pierre-Paul, who owned the house before her. Built in 1983, the property underwent major renovations in 2020 before Bhad Bhabie bought it two years later.

Her OnlyFans income helps explain how she could afford that purchase while still in her teens, based on figures she shared publicly.

An April 2022 house tour from Famous Entertainment offers a look at the Boca Raton property she bought that year.

After joining the platform in April 2021, she posted an earnings screenshot showing nearly $53 million in gross revenue the following year. That statement put her take after platform fees at roughly $43 million, a sum far above the mansion’s purchase price.

During a March 2025 stream with DDG, she put her running total even higher, according to Us Weekly.

“Now, overall, the net on it is like $75 million.”

Those earnings also came alongside another costly home purchase: Realtor.com reported she paid $5.15 million for a Tarzana property in September 2024.

She’s also putting out music, with her latest single, “What U Like,” released October 9 through Plush Records.

The release follows “Ms. Whitman,” her 2025 diss aimed at Alabama Barker during their bitter public feud. That track sampled “Carnival,” and she told DDG that Bianca Censori helped her secure Kanye West’s approval for its use.

She said she contacted Censori directly and received word that West had cleared the sample within about 10 minutes.

Marcy F. Javor of Signature One Luxury Estates is handling the Florida listing, which specifies six full bathrooms and one half bathroom.

item.title: Witness Says Lookout Stalked AKA In Restaurant Before Deadly Shooting
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: AKA's murder trial focused on CCTV that a witness said placed an accused lookout within sight of the rapper's restaurant table.
item.content:encoded:
AKA‘s murder trial put the man accused of watching the rapper inside Wish restaurant in focus Friday, October 23, when a police witness identified Lindokuhle Ndimande in security footage shown in court.

Rajen Sanders told the Durban High Court that Ndimande sat with a clear view of AKA’s table, according to SABC News. The rapper had been eating with his entourage before he was shot outside the restaurant.

Sanders also identified Ndimande as the person seen getting out of a car linked to co-defendant Mziwethemba Gwabeni near the venue. Prosecutor Lawrence Gcaba said he planned to submit records from Ndimande’s bail application, in which Ndimande acknowledged being at Wish.

Ndimande has given a different reason for being there.

During his 2024 bail application, he denied working as a spotter and said he was waiting for a woman to meet him for a date. He said his repeated calls were attempts to reach her after she failed to arrive, Daily Sun reported.

Friday’s footage followed his movements between Wish and nearby AuthentiQ restaurant. Daily Sun reported that he changed tables several times, allegedly to improve his view of AKA, before remaining on a call until the shooting.

Sanders said he downloaded the recordings and watched them repeatedly, identifying Ndimande as the man wearing shorts and a white T-shirt, according to TimesLIVE.

The footage placed him inside Wish when the shots were fired. He then stood up while still on his phone, paid his bill by card and left. AKA’s friend, Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane, had earlier been seated with friends at AuthentiQ, which Ndimande was also seen entering.

AKA and Tibz were killed outside Wish on Durban’s Florida Road on February 10, 2023. The rapper, whose real name was Kiernan Forbes, was 35.

The trial began on October 5. Friday’s hearing brought the court back to footage from the restaurants on the night of the killings.

Seven men are on trial. All pleaded not guilty to charges that include conspiracy to commit murder, two murders, five counts of attempted murder and firearm and ammunition offenses.

The trial was adjourned until Monday, when Sanders is due to continue his testimony about the video footage.

item.title: Blueface’s Alleged Fourth Baby Mama Breaks Down In Tears
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Blueface's alleged fourth baby mama, Rela, sparked abandonment rumors after crying on livestream, but she insists her tears weren't from sadness.
item.content:encoded:
Blueface has another pregnancy controversy brewing. I promise this has nothing to do with Chisean Rock.

This is about the woman claiming to carry his fifth child insists her emotional livestream wasn’t quite the heartbreak people think it was.

Here we go again!

Rela, also known as Rela Coleman or @relabaybee, has found herself in the middle of another Blueface situation. She claims she is pregnant with the rapper’s daughter and recently appeared on a livestream crying. Naturally, the internet wasted approximately three seconds before concluding that Blueface had abandoned another pregnant woman. I know I did.

But wait! Give him a second.

“it’s not sad tears trust me”

Those were Rela’s words, and they certainly complicate the narrative circulating online.

Social media chatter suggests that Rela has been dealing with Blueface’s alleged neglect during her pregnancy. He flat out said he has no intention of being involved in her life or the child’s upbringing. WOW. Hopefully that is not true since we have not confirmed yet.

Paternity is the elephant in the room.

Rela is not certain, but she has publicly expressed great confidence that Blueface is the father of her unborn daughter.

Blueface already has four children with three women, including Jaidyn Alexis, Chrisean Rock and Nevaeh Akira. If Rela’s claims are eventually confirmed, the rapper could be welcoming his fifth child with a fourth woman.

That’s quite a family tree for a man whose romantic relationships regularly resemble reality television reunions.

Blueface’s relationship with Chrisean Rock has provided enough drama for a few seasons of an episodic thriller. Their ongoing public drama is a lot especially when it comes to parenting.

The second we see woman associated with Blueface…we think bad.

But crying may not mean abandonment in this case. I mean, it probably does. It is not an established fact.

Will Blueface will address Rela’s pregnancy? For now, Rela says one thing. I do not think it is that.

Maybe she’s genuinely happy.

Stay tuned.

item.title: Too $hort’s Oakland Street Sign Goes Missing
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Too $hort's Oakland street sign went missing nearly four years after the city honored the rap legend beside his former school.
item.content:encoded:
Too $hort‘s street sign went missing from the Oakland corner where the city honored him.

Local reports placed the missing “Too Short Way” marker at the corner of Foothill Boulevard and High Street. Its cameras documented the sign’s absence. Oakland police treated the incident as a theft but have not provided details.

Oakland put up the marker after honoring the rapper in December 2022. The tribute covered three blocks of Foothill Boulevard, from High Street to 47th Avenue, beside the rapper’s former school, Fremont High.

The December 10, 2022 celebration brought Ice Cube, Mistah F.A.B. and Sway Calloway to Fremont’s gym. The Pittsburg High School marching band played Too $hort’s music as the crowd celebrated his place in the city’s history.

Then-Mayor Libby Schaaf and Councilmember Noel Gallo presented the city’s proclamation. Oakland also named that date “Too $hort Day.”

At the ceremony, he recalled listening to East Coast rap on long walks and wanting to tell Oakland’s stories in the same way.

When he addressed the crowd, the rapper made clear that he saw the day as a celebration of Oakland, not just himself. Fans followed him outside to see the new sign in the rain.

“This moment is not mine,” he said at the unveiling, according to KQED’s coverage. “This moment is Oakland, California.”

Too $hort used the occasion to announce plans to work with Oakland Unified School District, Affect The Youth and Fremont High to bring back marching bands and music programs.

That location held more than just his name on a pole. In an SFGATE interview, he described Fremont as the meeting point for friends who made tapes and then sold them around the neighborhood. He had moved to Oakland from Los Angeles as a teenager.

He also said he wanted young people to see that artists who faced the same hurdles had walked those streets and attended those schools. The honor was meant to offer them a path to imagine for themselves.
